requirements.reason: Current roster, capacity, waitlist, provider-adjacent, credit, refund, and financial database invariants must be cataloged with one authoritative disposition per invariant.
Community capacity decisions must serialize on the owning PostgreSQL game row before reading and deciding roster, waitlist, relationship, or capacity state.
Waitlist promotion must preserve full-party capacity, waitlist order, pending-payment holds, and fresh capacity recomputation after committed provider boundaries.
Capacity-mutating workflows, including multi-game account-deletion roster cleanup, must follow deterministic game-first lock order.
Active participant, waitlist, provider, and idempotency duplicates must be database-enforced with bounded conflict outcomes.
Current financial invariants must retain their frozen dispositions without broad payment/provider lifecycle redesign.
Game-credit concurrency must prevent overdrawing, double restoration, double reversal, and lost ledger rows.
Contention, integrity, lock timeout, deadlock, serialization, and unknown database outcomes must remain bounded without process-local locks or blind replay.
Accepted database foundations and WS04-02A transaction-boundary contracts must remain intact without final production infrastructure assumptions.
